name: Restore Power — Unreal C++ Quest Sample

6c069694-7fea-4980-b59d-d9dc2c857cc4.content:
WORLD EVENTS · read each lane from left to right

Unreal calls an entry point when the corresponding world event occurs. Connections inside a lane run automatically; unconnected lanes wait for their own event. Initialization never accepts the task.

Five global quest variables have distinct owners: questStarted and questCompleted are narrative milestones; powerRestored records the generator state; powerCells is the number of unique pickups collected by Unreal; requiredPowerCells is the authored target. The UI folder groups HUD text (hud), World text (world_text), and Quest display (quest_ui). Their nineteen scoped strings plus the five global quest variables make twenty-four runtime variables. Presentation refresh resets only quest_ui fields, preserving shared text overrides and quest state.

The collect_cell component requests a physical pickup. Unreal records that pickup, updates powerCells, and then follows the connection to the feedback element. restore_power and open_gate are registered C++ world actions. Completing the generator does not complete the quest: the player must enter the exit.

The Objectives and interface board chooses a cached display after each event. HUD drawing and focus queries only read that cache.

e1d06b05-73ac-4040-97d1-04a6f8091204.content:
INITIALIZE

Called once after importing fresh project defaults. Ends with arrival feedback; no automatic terminal interaction.

b7583d4b-fa40-4507-9057-7d2538281cc6.content:
TERMINAL EVENT

The terminal accepts the task once, then responds to accepted, powered, or completed state.

63297b78-e94e-4676-9e36-7dbdb9b02061.content:
GENERATOR EVENT

Check already-powered state first, then task acceptance, then the authored cell requirement. Success opens the gate; it does not finish the quest.

567ce162-983d-43ba-b0d6-409dce845e18.content:
PICKUP EVENT

Narrative permission precedes the collect_cell world action. Render feedback only after Unreal updates powerCells.

0bb7461c-3c0e-4337-8000-ef8c544dfd29.content:
PHYSICAL DUPLICATE EVENT

Unreal detects an already-collected world actor and executes this feedback directly. This physical fact needs no extra story variable.

8a1702ae-b5fe-44cb-bacd-97868065a17c.content:
EXIT EVENT

Called by the exit overlap. Only a powered exit can set questCompleted; repeated overlaps produce feedback without repeating completion.

617a47ca-5627-4dd4-a761-e4e9436af53c.content:
OBJECTIVE AND INTERACTION DISPLAY · defaults, then small overrides

The UI folder contains HUD text (hud), World text (world_text), and Quest display (quest_ui). Shared interface strings live in the first two components; the seven quest_ui attributes hold the authored default display.

Entry resets each quest_ui field individually, then this graph overrides only what changes for the current state. It never resets quest globals, hud, or world_text. Unaccepted changes two prompts; Ready changes the generator prompt. The shared Powered setup changes four fields for both powered outcomes; Completed adds its mission-heading override.

The five final leaves retain their objective text. C++ executes the path, then caches the current hud, world_text, and quest_ui values. HUD drawing and focus queries only read that cache. Each condition row has one outgoing connection.

For the released Unreal plugin, put each Arcscript reset or assignment in its own code block. Consecutive code blocks execute in order.
